subject: Proposal: Reserved capacity swap — offset schedule & SLA mapping
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mateo Ruiz <mateo@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — hosted credits conversion & sizing questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. We ran the usage export you requested (attached) — monthly avg is ~45M tokens for inference, with 95th percentile burst periods at ~320 concurrent requests (p50 latency target ~120ms currently). We're evaluating a move to Reserved (Dedicated) because predictable unit cost is critical for our product roadmap.

A few things we need clarity on before we schedule exec approvals:
- How do hosted credits convert to committed months? Are there set conversion ratios or sliding offsets?
- Do you offer bridge months (partial refunds or credits) while we ramp our Dedicated pool?
- Sizing: what's the recommended GPU pool for our workload (batch vs real-time mix is ~70/30)? We'd like a 99% latency SLO at the committed throughput.
- Pricing: any tiered discounts for 12 vs 24 vs 36 month commits, and what discounts are available for upfront payment?

Can you send a proposal that maps our current hosted spend to a Reserved commit option and a proposed offset schedule? Ideally a few options (conservative / balanced / aggressive) so we can take to procurement.

Appended: usage-report-q3.csv (token counts + burst windows).

Best,
Jenna Park
Head of Platform
Acme Analytics
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Mateo Ruiz <mateo@acmeanalytics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — hosted credits conversion & sizing questions

Hi Jenna — thanks for the upload, that helps a lot. I reviewed the CSV quickly and looped in Neha (your account lead) to coordinate pricing and scheduling. High-level answers below; I'll follow with a formal proposal PDF and an offset schedule by EOD Monday.

1) Conversion / offset model: we offer a conversion-credit schedule tied to remaining hosted credits and the commit length. Typical structure: 1) a one-time conversion credit applied toward the first 3 months of the Reserved commit (scaled by remaining hosted credits), and 2) a staged offset that reduces the first 6 months of invoice for customers with active hosted spend. Exact ratios vary by commit length — I will include conservative/balanced/aggressive examples.

2) Bridge months: yes — we can structure 1–3 bridge months where you run both environments and receive partial credit on hosted charges. Bridge months are often used when traffic reroutes gradually.

3) GPU pool sizing / SLO mapping: preliminary recommendation for your profile (70% batch, 30% RT, 45M tokens/mo, spikes to ~320 concurrent): a mixed pool using A10x8 + T4x4 (or A10x12 if you prefer a single-family approach) with a throughput target that maps to 120–150 RPS sustained and 350 RPS burst capability. That supports a 99% latency SLO at ~120ms with continuous batching enabled. Sean will add technical notes on kernel selection and KV-cache sizing.

4) Pricing tiers: 12/24/36 month commits — discounts increase with term (baseline: 20% off hosted unit-price at 12 months, 28% at 24, 35% at 36 with additional 3–7% for upfront). We'll quantify in the proposal.

Next steps: Neha will propose a formal offset schedule and draft the term language for the Reserved order. Can we schedule a 45-minute sync next week (Mon/Tue preferred)?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Jenna Park <jenna@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mateo Ruiz <mateo@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — hosted credits conversion & sizing questions

Vanessa,

Appreciate the quick summary. A couple clarifications before the call:
- Our legal team will want any bridge-credit mechanics spelled out in the order form (cap on total credits, recapture events, etc.). Expect them to loop in legal@acmeanalytics.com.
- For SLOs: we actually need 99.9% for one of our premium routes. Can you confirm the pooling approach still supports that with auto-burst and fallback to hosted during outages?
- For the conversion credit: does it reduce the committed capacity (i.e., we buy fewer months) or is it simply a credit applied to invoices?

If you can include an option that preserves capacity (credit applied to invoices rather than reducing months) we'll push this faster.

—Jenna
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@acmeanalytics.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — hosted credits conversion & sizing questions

Hi Jenna — Sean from SE here. Two technical notes to make the SLA mapping concrete:

1) Pool topology: for a 99.9% SLO on the premium route, we recommend separating that route onto an isolated subpool (A10x4) within the Dedicated reservation to avoid noisy-neighbor interference. The rest of traffic can sit in shared pools.

2) Fallback strategy: we support a policy that routes to the hosted fleet on spike or sustained capacity shortages. That is implemented as an automated policy (region/latency/cost priority) and can be used as a safety valve during the ramp. Fallbacks are chargeable at hosted rates unless we agree to a capped temporary extension in the contract.

3) Conversion credits: operationally we apply credits as invoice line items; we do not reduce committed GPU months. This keeps your capacity guarantees intact while easing cashflow during ramp.

I'll include a short appendix in the proposal that maps your token profile to expected GPU utilization and KV-cache sizing.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@acmeanalytics.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Legal <legal@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood proposal & commercial terms (RWD-ACME-2026)

Hi Jenna and team — attaching the formal proposal PDF with two commercial options: 24-month balanced commit and 36-month aggressive commit. Highlights:
- Conversion credit structure: one-time credit equal to 40% of remaining hosted pre-paid credits applied across the first 3 invoice cycles (invoice credit line).
- Bridge months: we offer up to 2 bridge months with a 50% credit on hosted overage charges during that period.
- Discounting: 24-month: 28% off baseline unit price + 3% upfront payment discount. 36-month: 35% off + 5% upfront.
- SLA guarantees: 99.9% uptime for dedicated control plane and documented latency SLOs per route. Remedies and credits defined in Exhibit B.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-RWD-ACME-2026.pdf (proposal + draft order form). Please review and share any redlines.

If the bridge-month credit cap or the conversion ratio needs to be different for your procurement, let us know — we're open to adjusting based on committed capacity.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood proposal & commercial terms (RWD-ACME-2026)

Jenna — following up to see if you had time to review Rishi's proposal. Proposed immediate actions:
- Internal legal review (Acme) + our standard order form redlines (we can accept most commercial asks but will need minor adjustments to Exhibit B on remedies).
- Schedule 45-minute alignment call Thursday to finalize the offset schedule and sign-off on bridge months. I'll invite the appropriate execs.
- If you want to preserve capacity, confirm you want credits as invoice offsets (as Sean described) — we'll reflect that in the order.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
